questions.text: In Excel, A2:A10 holds departments and B2:B10 holds salaries. Which formula counts employees of the 'Sales' department earning more than 50000?
questions.explanation: COUNTIFS takes several range-criterion pairs and counts rows meeting all of them.
steps: Spot what the question tests: COUNTIF vs COUNTIFS.
Option A (=COUNTIF(A2:A10,"Sales",B2:B10,">50000")) is out: COUNTIF accepts only one range and one criterion.
Option B (=SUMIFS(B2:B10,A2:A10,"Sales",B2:B10,">50000")) is out: Returns the total salary, not the count.
Option C (=COUNTA(A2:A10,"Sales")) is out: Counts non-empty cells, ignoring the criteria.
Common slip to avoid: Using COUNTIF with two pairs.
So the answer is option D: =COUNTIFS(A2:A10,"Sales",B2:B10,">50000").
wrongReasons: COUNTIF accepts only one range and one criterion
Returns the total salary, not the count
Counts non-empty cells, ignoring the criteria

questions.text: In Excel, what is the result of =ROUND(-2.5,0)?
questions.explanation: Excel's ROUND rounds halves away from zero, so -2.5 becomes -3.
steps: Spot what the question tests: ROUND behaviour.
Option A (-2) is out: Excel does not round half to even.
Option B (-2.5) is out: No rounding applied.
Option D (3) is out: Sign is lost.
Common slip to avoid: Applying banker's rounding.
So the answer is option C: -3.
wrongReasons: Excel does not round half to even

questions.text: Which tab in MS Excel contains the Freeze Panes command?
questions.explanation: Freeze Panes is in the Window group of the View tab.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Excel ribbon tabs.
Option A (Home) is out: Holds formatting and clipboard tools.
Option B (Data) is out: Holds sorting and filtering tools.
Option C (Page Layout) is out: Holds page setup tools.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Page Layout.
So the answer is option D: View.

questions.text: In MS Word, to make one page landscape while the rest remain portrait, which should be inserted around that page?
questions.explanation: A section break lets a section have its own orientation.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Breaks in Word.
Option A (Page breaks) is out: They start a new page but keep the same page setup.
Option B (Column breaks) is out: They affect text columns only.
Option D (Text wrapping breaks) is out: They affect text flow around objects.
Common slip to avoid: Using a page break.
So the answer is option C: Section breaks.
wrongReasons: They start a new page but keep the same page setup
They affect text flow around objects

questions.text: In MS PowerPoint, which key starts the slide show from the first slide?
questions.explanation: F5 starts the show from the beginning; Shift + F5 starts it from the current slide.
steps: F5 runs from slide 1
Shift + F5 runs from the selected slide

questions.text: A fraudulent attempt to steal information through SMS text messages is called:
questions.explanation: Smishing combines SMS and phishing.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Phishing variants.
Option A (Vishing) is out: Done over voice calls.
Option B (Pharming) is out: Redirects users through DNS or host changes.
Option C (Spoofing) is out: Impersonation in general.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing vishing.
So the answer is option D: Smishing.
wrongReasons: Redirects users through DNS or host changes

questions.text: Which of the following is an asymmetric-key algorithm?
questions.explanation: RSA uses a public key and a private key.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Symmetric vs asymmetric.
Options A and B are out: A symmetric block cipher.
Option D (RC4) is out: A symmetric stream cipher.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing AES.
So the answer is option C: RSA.

questions.text: A Distributed Denial of Service attack mainly compromises which element of the CIA triad?
questions.explanation: It floods a service so that legitimate users cannot reach it.
steps: Spot what the question tests: CIA triad.
Option B (Confidentiality) is out: Concerns unauthorised disclosure.
Option C (Integrity) is out: Concerns unauthorised modification.
Option D (Authenticity) is out: Not a part of the triad.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing confidentiality.
So the answer is option A: Availability.
wrongReasons: Not a part of the triad

questions.text: Which CPU register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.explanation: The Program Counter points to the next instruction.
steps: Spot what the question tests: CPU registers.
Option A (Instruction Register) is out: Holds the instruction being executed.
Option C (Accumulator) is out: Holds arithmetic results.
Option D (Memory Data Register) is out: Holds the data read or written.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the Instruction Register.
So the answer is option B: Program Counter.
wrongReasons: Holds the data read or written

questions.text: What is the 8-bit two's complement representation of the binary number 00010110?
questions.explanation: Invert to 11101001 and add 1 to get 11101010.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Two's complement.
Option B (11101001) is out: This is the one's complement.
Option C (11101011) is out: One more than the correct value.
Option D (10010110) is out: Only the sign bit is changed.
Common slip to avoid: Stopping at the one's complement.
So the answer is option A: 11101010.
wrongReasons: One more than the correct value
Only the sign bit is changed

questions.text: What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number (3F)₁₆?
steps: Spot what the question tests: Hex to decimal.
Option B (48) is out: Counts only the 3 in the sixteens place.
Option C (18) is out: Adds the digits.
Option D (255) is out: This is (FF)₁₆.
Common slip to avoid: Adding digits instead of weighting.
So the answer is option A: 63.
wrongReasons: Counts only the 3 in the sixteens place

questions.text: Which of the following is a private IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: The private ranges are 10.x.x.x, 172.16.x.x to 172.31.x.x and 192.168.x.x.
steps: 172.16 to 172.31 is private
172.20 falls in that range

questions.text: The IP address 172.16.5.4 belongs to which class?
questions.explanation: A first octet of 128 to 191 means Class B.
steps: Spot what the question tests: IP address classes.
Option A (Class A) is out: First octet 1 to 126.
Option B (Class C) is out: First octet 192 to 223.
Option C (Class D) is out: First octet 224 to 239, used for multicast.
Common slip to avoid: Misjudging the range.
So the answer is option D: Class B.
wrongReasons: First octet 224 to 239, used for multicast

questions.text: Which port number is used by the Secure Shell (SSH) protocol by default?
questions.explanation: SSH runs on TCP port 22.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Well-known ports.
Option B (23) is out: Used by Telnet.
Option C (21) is out: Used by FTP.
Option D (25) is out: Used by SMTP.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Telnet's port.
So the answer is option A: 22.

questions.text: How many usable host addresses are there in the network 192.168.1.0/27?
questions.explanation: A /27 leaves 5 host bits: 2^5 - 2 = 30.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Host count formula.
Option A (32) is out: Includes the network and broadcast addresses.
Option B (31) is out: Subtracts only one address.
Option D (62) is out: This is for a /26 network.
Common slip to avoid: Forgetting the network and broadcast addresses.
So the answer is option C: 30.
questions.trap: Forgetting the network and broadcast addresses.
wrongReasons: Includes the network and broadcast addresses

questions.text: What is the lowest normal form that eliminates transitive dependencies of non-key attributes on the primary key?
questions.explanation: 3NF removes transitive dependencies.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Normal forms.
Option A (First normal form) is out: Deals with atomic values.
Option C (Second normal form) is out: Deals with partial dependencies.
Option D (Fourth normal form) is out: A higher form dealing with multivalued dependencies.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing 2NF.
So the answer is option B: Third normal form.
wrongReasons: A higher form dealing with multivalued dependencies

questions.text: A table has 10 rows and the column Phone contains NULL in 3 of them. What does SELECT COUNT(Phone) return?
questions.explanation: COUNT(column) ignores NULL values.
steps: Spot what the question tests: COUNT(*) vs COUNT(column).
Option A (10) is out: This is COUNT(*).
Option B (3) is out: Counts the NULLs.
Option C (0) is out: NULLs are not all values.
Common slip to avoid: Confusing it with COUNT(*).
So the answer is option D: 7.

questions.text: Which memory management technique divides memory into fixed-size blocks called frames?
questions.explanation: Paging splits physical memory into frames and logical memory into pages.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Paging vs segmentation.
Option A (Segmentation) is out: Uses variable-sized logical units.
Option C (Swapping) is out: Moves processes between memory and disk.
Option D (Compaction) is out: Joins free memory areas.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing segmentation.
So the answer is option B: Paging.
wrongReasons: Moves processes between memory and disk

questions.text: In cloud computing, which model gives developers a platform to build and run applications without managing the underlying servers?
questions.explanation: PaaS provides the runtime environment and tools.
steps: Spot what the question tests: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS.
Option A (Infrastructure as a Service) is out: Gives virtual machines and storage.
Option C (Software as a Service) is out: Gives finished applications.
Option D (Network as a Service) is out: Gives network connectivity.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing IaaS.
So the answer is option B: Platform as a Service.

questions.text: Which key combination locks a Windows computer immediately?
questions.explanation: Windows key + L locks the session.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Windows shortcuts.
Option B (Windows key + D) is out: Shows the desktop.
Option C (Ctrl + Alt + L) is out: Not a lock shortcut.
Option D (Windows key + R) is out: Opens the Run box.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the desktop shortcut.
So the answer is option A: Windows key + L.
